title: Quack durable session documents
description: The five pi-durable documents a quack session keeps in its durable store beside its run: quack.artifacts (sealed artifact versions), quack.approvals (gated tool calls awaiting or holding a verdict), quack.questions (questions escalated to a person), quack.failures (where the latest run ended) and quack.workflow (the latest run's steps). Each stored value is one of the five $defs; which one is fixed by the document's kind string stored beside the value, not by a field in the value. Objects at every level are open (additionalProperties: true): stored documents outlive the code that wrote them, so a reader skips unknown fields and treats a field added by later code as possibly absent. Sealed from now: this schema describes documents written from this version on; stored documents are not re-validated, and a reader must tolerate values older code produced (e.g. a workflow step of kind 'gated', removed in f7e32ff5 #2275) without crashing.

epochMillis.description: A time as an integer of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as written by api.now() or Date.now(); the lifecycle channel renders it as RFC 3339 only on the wire.

principal.description: Who acted: a named person, a tailnet caller, or a bare name string in a record written before principals were typed (the SDK's principalName resolves all three).

name.description: The person's name; the session server requires a non-empty name.

anyOf.description: A tailnet caller. Closed, unlike the person branch: the SDK's tailnet principal (repo/packages/sdk/src/principal.ts:2) has no other field, and a name beside a tailnet kind would read as a person.

sealedArtifact.description: A version of one kind's artifact at the instant it was sealed: the sha256 of content as hash, the content itself, and what the run concluded (outcome is a note, e.g. contracts' `v6` - nothing enforces a length). Links, a checker's verdict and the finalization are attached to the version after the fact; the content and hash never change.

kind.description: The name of the artifact kind this version belongs to, as declared by the session's artifacts extension.

version.description: This version's ordinal within its kind, one-based; sealing content unchanged from the latest version returns that version instead of a new one.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the sealed content, lowercase hex; identical content keeps its version.

content.description: The exact content of the workspace file as sealed; it never changes on a version — a link and the verdict attach to the version without touching it.

sealedAt.description: When this version was sealed, in epoch milliseconds; unchanged when a link or verdict is attached to the version.

verdict.description: What a checker (and any seal gates) recorded: an opaque object with the keys the checker and gates wrote (run, passed, limitReached, score, gatesFailed, rubric, checks, undecided), or null until checked. This schema does not define its fields; the judge and rubric own them.

links.description: Pointers an extension attaches after sealing, e.g. where the version was delivered; omitted when there are none, and a repeated URL is not added twice.

outcome.description: A short reading of the sealed content (a review's verdict, a contract's version), stored on the version so lists need not fetch content; nothing enforces a length.

summary.description: One line of what the content concluded, or undefined until the summarizer attaches one; cut to 80 chars (SUMMARY_MAX). May be the empty string: contracts' reconcile writes note.slice(0, 80), which is empty for a rejection with no reason.

basis.description: What the version was written against (a review's head commit), stored so a viewer can tell when it has been overtaken.

final.description: Set by the SDK's seal tool on a judged version every gate passed: input is the run's newest input id (a SubmissionId as a string) at delivery, and refused counts the changed seals refused since the version became final, starting at 0. While input is still the run's newest input, a changed seal of that kind is refused - first as a continue, then as a deny that ends the run - and a new input to the run reopens it. Optional, never null: the SDK writes the object or leaves the key absent.

examples.summary: Ship: the regression is fixed and the report passes.

artifactLink.description: A pointer an extension attaches to a sealed version after the fact, e.g. where it was delivered.

label.description: The where, in words: what the version was delivered to.

url.description: The link itself; a repeated URL is not attached twice.

versions.description: The kind's sealed versions, oldest first.

artifactsDoc.description: quack.artifacts: the sealed artifact versions a session has produced, grouped by kind.

kinds.description: The session's artifact kinds, keyed by kind name; a kind is absent until its first seal.

approvalVerdict.description: A person's decision on a gated tool call; recorded once, never overwritten — resolving an unknown or already-decided approval is refused.

decision.description: Whether the call may run; the session's HTTP API accepts nothing else.

reason.description: The person's words for the decision; null when they gave none.

by.description: Who decided: a person, a tailnet caller, or a bare name string in a record written before principals were typed.

at.description: When the decision was recorded, in epoch milliseconds.

approval.description: A gated tool call and its state: opened with the call's arguments, decided by a person, then executed exactly once.

tool.description: The name of the gated tool that requested the approval.

args.description: The arguments the tool was called with, as JSON; any JSON value.

requestedAt.description: When the gated call opened its approval, in epoch milliseconds.

verdict.description: The person's decision; null while the call is pending, after which it is fixed.

executing.description: True once the approved call has started execution, so a crash mid-execution is reported instead of re-running the side effect.

done.description: True once the approved call has finished.

approvalsDoc.description: quack.approvals: the gated tool calls awaiting or holding a person's decision.

items.description: Keyed by String(api.taskId) of the gated tool call, one approval per call; a session can hold several (a prod session holds approvals 96, 113, 125, 190, 211 and 222).

questionAnswer.description: A person's answer to a question; the first answer stands.

choice.description: The option label chosen, or — for a free-text answer — the person's words, which text then repeats.

by.description: Who answered: a person, a tailnet caller, or a bare name string in a record written before principals were typed.

at.description: When the answer was recorded, in epoch milliseconds; the first answer stands, later ones are refused.

note.description: A note the person added to a listed choice; at most 2000 characters (MAX_ANSWER_CHARS).

text.description: The person's own words; present only on a free-text answer, at most 2000 characters.

question.description: A question a run escalated to a person, with the card copy it was asked with and its answer; the last resolver of a decision chain is a person.

options.description: The option labels an answer must match one of, unless the question is free text.

evidence.description: The evidence offered with the question; null when there was none.

header.description: A short chip naming the topic; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

title.description: The question as a headline; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

detail.description: One to three sentences of context; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

optionDescriptions.description: One line (the trade-off) per option label; {} when the question named none; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

suggested.description: The index into options of the recommended choice; null when none was recommended; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

freeText.description: Whether the question accepts the person's own words, or a note on a listed option; false when the question opted out; absent on questions stored before these card fields existed.

askedAt.description: When the question was asked, in epoch milliseconds.

answer.description: The person's answer; null until it stands — the first answer wins, later ones are refused.

closed.description: True when the run that asked ended without an answer, so nobody is waiting on it; an answer is refused on a closed question.

examples.question: Which branch ships?
examples.evidence: main is one commit ahead of release/2.0.
examples.title: Choose the ship branch
examples.detail: main is one commit ahead of release/2.0.

questionsDoc.description: quack.questions: the questions escalated to a person, beside quack.approvals — written by whichever extension escalates, served and indexed generically.

items.description: Keyed by <task id>:<question name> - String(api.taskId) plus the question point's name - one entry per question point asked by a run.

failureRow.description: What the latest run ended on for one step: a failed run leaves no transcript, so this is where its error shows; a later run's clean row supersedes an earlier failure.

error.description: The error a run ended on; null while the run reached this step and got through it — a clean run clears its row.

run.description: The id of the run that wrote this row, as a number; it orders rows so a later run's clean one supersedes an earlier failure.

at.description: When the row was written, in epoch milliseconds; 0 on a row startWorkflow or resumeWorkflow opened before a failure, while the 'model' row instead carries a real timestamp.

failuresDoc.description: quack.failures: where the latest run ended, for the session view and the index.

items.description: Keyed by step name, by 'runaway' for a run the runtime aborted, and by 'model' for the model-fault path; startWorkflow replaces items wholesale, dropping earlier 'runaway' and 'model' rows.

stepProgress.description: How far a step has worked through its units (pages).

done.description: How many units the step has finished.

total.description: How many units the step works through in all.

stepRecord.description: One step of the latest run, as the session view renders it: its status, duration and cost.

name.description: The step's name, unique within the workflow.

kind.description: The step's nature: the four kinds the workflow engine runs. Closed: adding or renaming a kind is a breaking change. The kind 'gated' (it existed from #1872 to #2275) is not accepted here; stored documents are not re-validated, and no reader switches on kind.

status.description: Where the step is in its run; 'waiting' is a step blocked on a person, and aborting the run moves a waiting step to 'aborted'. A step interrupted by a close stays 'running' and resumes.

startedAt.description: When the step started its run; null while it is still pending.

durationMs.description: How long the step took, in milliseconds, from start to end; null until it ends.

cost.description: The spend the step has accumulated so far, the sum of its model calls' usage.cost.total as reported by the engine; 0 for a code step.

progress.description: The units a step works through (pages); absent on records written before it existed, null once set and not yet reported.

error.description: The error that failed the step; null unless the step failed.

workflowDoc.description: quack.workflow: what the session view renders for the latest run — each step's status, duration and cost.

name.description: The workflow's declared name; null before the session's first run.

task.description: The task id of the latest run, as a string; null before the first run. A resume starts a new task and replaces it.

request.description: The person's request that started the latest run; null when it named none.

steps.description: The steps of the latest run in declared order; a resume splices in from the failed step, keeping the earlier records.

kept.description: The results of the steps before a failed one, so a resume starts from them; set on failure, left in place after a resume, reset to null only by a new run. Absent on records written before it existed.

additionalProperties.description: The step's stored result; any JSON value.

input.description: The run's newest input id (a SubmissionId as a string) at delivery.

refused.description: The changed seals refused since the version became final; starts at 0.
